newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends up broadly amid late surge.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends up broadly amid late surge.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures surged at the session's close as buy stops were hit, and the market settled broadly higher on a mix of bullish inputs, traders said.

Traders said late buying was broad-based, with funds and commercials joining the fray. One trader said the market feared that weekend rains in North Dakota would be excessive and could increase the risk of damage and disease to the crop.
"What a close," a MGE trader exclaimed. "We had a six-cent (per bushel) closing range. We even triggered a 500,000-bushel stop on the close."

Wheat also gained on spillover from CBOT corn and soybean futures, which strengthened after forecasters indicated that much-needed rains this weekend would likely fall north of dry growing regions in the U.S. Midwest.
MGE spring wheat settled 7-1/2 to 13 cents per bushel higher, with new crop September up 8-3/4 cents at $3.79-1/4. December was up 7-1/4 cents at $3.80-1/2.

Traders said ADM's Benson-Quinn commodity division bought two million Sept bushels, of which 800,000 was done on the close. Benson-Quinn has been the featured buyer all week in the MGE Sept spring wheat contract.
Atwood-Peavey, Country Hedging and Linnco Futures each bought around 1.5 million Sept on the day, traders said.
The MGE estimated Friday's volume at 23.5 million bushels, up from Thursday's volume of 18.56 million bushels.
